newsitem.title: USA: Edward Jones settles SEC charges in UIT case.
newsitem.headline: Edward Jones settles SEC charges in UIT case.

text.p: Edward Jones agreed to pay $50,000 to settle SEC allegations that it failed to tell investors it could charge commissions for repurchasing units of unit investment trusts (UITs), the commission said Tuesday.
According to Securities and Exchange Commmission, the firm maintained a secondary market since 1989 for units in three UITs - Insured Tax-Free Income Trust, the Equity Trust and 21st Century Trust.
As part of its program, the firm offered to repurchase units from investors at their net asset value (NAV), SEC said.
Company prospectuses pledged to purchase the units at the same price at which they could be redeemed - the units' NAV, SEC said.
Documents also said the company could keep, as profit, the difference between the purchase and resale price of the units, SEC said.
But investors were not told that the firm could charge a commission when purchasing the units from investors, SEC said.
Edward Jones, formerly Edward D. Jones & Co., made $120,000 in commissions, which were authorized by Donald Walter, the firm's compliance director since 1984, SEC said.
SEC said Tuesday that Edward Jones agreed to settle the matter without admitting or denying charges.
The firm agreed to pay a civil penalty of $50,000. And both the firm and Walter agreed to cease and desist from further violations.
SEC said that in September 1996, the firm began refunding the commissions, plus interest, to all investors, for a total of $198,111.
Officials at the firm were unavailable for comment.
